ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a solution container, with the liquid surface at the top; the solution is labeled with K+, NO3−, and Ag+, and there is a solid precipitate at the bottom, labeled Ag2SO4. From this it can be seen that the products indeed include a solid silver sulfate precipitate, while K+ and NO3− still exist as dissolved spectator ions. Reasoning: Ag2SO4(s) ⇌ 2Ag+(aq) + SO4^2−(aq), so Ksp = [Ag+]^2[SO4^2−]. The problem gives Ksp = 1.0 × 10^-5. Check [Ag+] = 0.10 M and [SO4^2−] = 0.01 M: Qsp = (0.10)^2(0.01) = 1.0 × 10^-4. Because Qsp > Ksp, that is, 1.0 × 10^-4 > 1.0 × 10^-5, these ion concentrations will cause Ag2SO4 to precipitate, matching the situation in the figure where Ag2SO4 solid appears at the bottom.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and note that a bottom solid labeled Ag2SO4 is present, while K+ and NO3− remain dissolved spectator ions. From the text, take Ksp = 1.0 × 10^-5 for Ag2SO4. Test the proposed concentrations [Ag+] = 0.10 M and [SO4^2−] = 0.01 M by computing Qsp = (0.10)^2(0.01) = 1.0 × 10^-4. Since Qsp > 1.0 × 10^-5, the mixture would precipitate Ag2SO4, matching the image; report those concentrations.
